Reading complete and findings verified against source. Three substantiated issues, all in the Types & API-contract lane.

1. [SEVERITY: minor] src/outcomes.ts:51 — `collect`'s discriminated-union switch is not exhaustiveness-checked
   Why: `collect` returns `T | undefined`, so `undefined` is already in the return type. The `switch (spec.kind)` (lines 52–59) has no `default`/`assertNever`. If a new `OutputSpec` kind is added to the union (types.ts:46–50), the switch silently falls through to an implicit `return undefined` with **no compile error** — the collector quietly no-ops for the new kind instead of forcing the author to handle it. Contrast `buildWorkflow` (index.ts) whose `(s): StepDefinition` return type *does* enforce exhaustiveness.
   Fix: add `default: { const _exhaustive: never = spec; throw new Error(`unknown OutputSpec kind: ${JSON.stringify(_exhaustive)}`); }` so a new kind is a compile error.

2. [SEVERITY: minor] src/index.ts:9 — `StepExecContext` is exported as public API but is internal runner plumbing
   Why: `StepExecContext` (stage-executor.ts:57) is the mutable per-run state the runner threads between steps — `dispatch`, `registry`, `journal: Journal`, `pool: BudgetPool`, plus mutable `spawned`/`depth` counters. It is never accepted by any public signature (`RunWorkflowOptions` takes `dispatch`/`registry`, not a context) and never returned from `runWorkflow` (`RunResult` doesn't expose it); it is only constructed at runner/index.ts:66. Exporting it pulls the otherwise-unexported `Journal` and `BudgetPool` types transitively into the public contract and couples external consumers to unstable engine internals. `AgentDispatch` (the legitimate injection seam) is the only type on that line that belongs in the barrel.
   Fix: `export { type AgentDispatch } from "./runner/stage-executor.ts";` — drop `StepExecContext`.

3. [SEVERITY: minor] src/index.ts:7 — `export *` leaks reserved/unimplemented fusion types (notably `AgentAbortMap`)
   Why: `export * from "./types.ts"` re-exports everything, including the "Claude Code fusion — reserved types (land in Tasks 3–5)" block. `AgentAbortMap` (types.ts:242) and `AgentCallId` (types.ts:232) are referenced **nowhere** outside their own definitions (grep confirms zero usages in `src/` or `index.ts`); per-agent abort was actually implemented via `AgentSpawnRegistry` in `sessions/spawn.ts`, not via this map. So `AgentAbortMap` is a dead, misleading type now baked into the public surface. `StepRetry.retryStage` (types.ts:184, "NOT YET IMPLEMENTED") is similarly exported as a live field.
   Fix: replace `export *` with an explicit allow-list of the intended public types (`WorkflowDefinition`, `StepDefinition` and the 7 step interfaces, `Budget`, `RunResult`, `RunStatus`, `StepResult`, `StepStats`, `StepContext`, `defineWorkflow`, `AgentOpts`), and drop `AgentAbortMap`/`AgentCallId` (or mark them internal and stop re-exporting).

I have completed a full read of all src files (`index.ts`, `types.ts`, `persistence.ts`, `state.ts`, `parse.ts`, `render.ts`, `internal-patch.ts`) plus targeted verification. Note: the pre-existing `audit-report.md` cites dead symbols (`firstMeaningfulLine`, `firstSentence`, `stepHeader`, `stripInlineFormattingMarkers`, `patchReleases`) that do **not** exist in the current code — I verified those are stale and excluded them. Below are the issues I independently substantiated against the current source.

1. [SEVERITY: minor] parse.ts:249 — `SUCCESS_CUE_RE` is dead code (zero references anywhere, not even tests).
   Why: The constant is declared but never read; `hasExplicitSuccessCue` (parse.ts:277) uses `EXPLICIT_SUCCESS_RESULT_RE` instead. Dead regex that future editors will assume is load-bearing.
   Fix: Delete the `const SUCCESS_CUE_RE` line.

2. [SEVERITY: minor] internal-patch.ts:134 — `hasVisibleThinkingContent` is an orphan function (defined, never called, not exported).
   Why: The patched `updateContent` uses `collectThinkingBlocks` + `hasVisibleTextContent`, never this helper. It rots silently and misleads readers about the visibility check used in rendering.
   Fix: Delete the function.

3. [SEVERITY: major] state.ts:30-49, 71-80, 110, 113, 137-144 — `LegacyThinkingUIGlobalState`, the `legacyMode` parameter, and the `state.mode`/`state.active`/`legacyActive` migration are speculative backward-compatibility for a prior globalThis state shape that no current code path writes.
   Why: This module is the sole writer of `globalThis[Symbol.for("pi-extensions.thinking-ui.state")]` and it always writes the per-scope shape. The legacy top-level `mode`/`active` fields would only appear if a *previous extension version* had populated the symbol in the same process — an unsupported upgrade path. ~30 lines (a whole redeclared-as-`unknown` interface + the `legacyMode` threading through `normalizeModeByScopeKey` + the `if (legacyActive.active)` block) exist purely to preserve that old shape, contradicting `AGENTS.md` ("Do not preserve backward compatibility unless the user asks for it") and obscuring `ensureGlobalStateShape`'s real (field-completion) job.
   Fix: Drop `mode`/`active` from `LegacyThinkingUIGlobalState`, remove the `legacyMode` param and the `??= normalizeThinkingMode(legacyMode)` seed, and delete the `legacyActive` block. Keep the `isRecord`/`instanceof` guards (those defend the persisted global state); collapse the legacy interface to `Partial<ThinkingUIGlobalState>` or an `unknown`+`isRecord` narrow.

4. [SEVERITY: minor] internal-patch.ts:210, 231, 251 — `fallbackToOriginalUpdateContent` / `…SetHideThinkingBlock` / `…SetHiddenThinkingLabel` are three copies of the same try/`withOriginalInstanceMethods`/catch-throw/`reportFallback` skeleton (~45 lines), differing only in the original method, the argument, and the stage label.
   Why: Any change to the error-cause shape or reporting must be made in three places. The first function takes a `stage` parameter while the other two hardcode their stage string — an inconsistency that already hints at the copy-paste drift.
   Fix: Extract one helper `runWithFallback(stage: string, originalError: unknown | undefined, run: () => void)` containing the shared try/catch/report, and have each call site pass a thunk invoking its specific original method.

5. [SEVERITY: minor] render.ts:283-285 — `renderThinkingInlineMarkup` calls `sanitizeThinkingText(text)` then passes the result to `parseThinkingInlineSegments`, which sanitizes *again* internally (render.ts:64).
   Why: Redundant work on every inline render, and ownership of sanitization is ambiguous (callers cannot tell whether `parseThinkingInlineSegments` expects pre-sanitized input).
   Fix: Have `parseThinkingInlineSegments` own the sanitization (remove the `sanitized` line in `renderThinkingInlineMarkup` and pass `text` directly), or remove the internal sanitize and document that callers must pre-sanitize — pick one.

6. [SEVERITY: minor] index.ts:290, index.ts:328, state.ts:316, state.ts:331 — the `typeof (x as { timestamp?: unknown }).timestamp === "number" ? (x as { timestamp: number }).timestamp : undefined` extraction is duplicated verbatim four times.
   Why: The same unsafe cast + narrowing is re-derived in every message handler and both scope helpers; a change to how `timestamp` is read must touch four spots.
   Fix: Extract a `readMessageTimestamp(message: object): number | undefined` helper and call it everywhere.

7. [SEVERITY: minor] parse.ts:363-381 — `compressCandidate` ends with 20 consecutive `.replace(/^gerund\b/i, "Imperative")` calls.
   Why: Pure data expressed as code — adding or correcting a gerund→imperative mapping requires a whole new `.replace()` line that re-scans from the start, and the table is hard to scan for completeness.
   Fix: Replace with a single `const IMPERATIVE: Record<string,string> = { using:"Use", inspecting:"Inspect", … }` lookup applied via one `candidate.replace(/^[a-z]+(?:\s+out)?/i, w => IMPERATIVE[w.toLowerCase()] ?? w)` (plus the special `connect and orient ourselves` / `look into` cases).

I have read all five files in full (`ast-guard.ts`, `key.ts`, `journal.ts`, `loader.ts`, `names.ts`) plus the wiring in `runner/index.ts`, `runner/stage-executor.ts`, `types.ts`, and `index.ts` to substantiate findings.

1. [blocker] src/loader.ts:37 + src/runner/index.ts:57-82 — The determinism AST guard is never enforced on the engine's primary entry point.
  Why: `assertDeterministic` is called in exactly one place — `loadWorkflowModule` (loader.ts:37). The public engine entry `runWorkflow` (runner/index.ts) takes an in-memory `WorkflowDefinition` object and never imports or calls the guard (its imports are fs/path/BudgetPool/Journal/generateRunId/spawn only). `loadWorkflowModule` has zero non-test callers, and every real caller (examples/smoke-real-pi.ts:29, index.ts:226, all of test/e2e) builds the workflow inline and passes it straight to `runWorkflow`. So a workflow whose `prompt`/`transform` function calls `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` runs unchallenged, its derived `CacheKey` (key.ts) varies every run, and journal resume (`Journal.lookup`) never replays — the cache-resume guarantee the guard is meant to underwrite is silently broken on the only path users actually take.
  Fix: Either make `runWorkflow` require a `filePath` and load through `loadWorkflowModule` (so the guard always runs before dispatch), or treat inline-object workflows as non-cacheable (skip journal write/lookup) so a bypassed guard cannot silently corrupt resume. As-is the guard is decorative on the main API.

2. [major] src/determinism/ast-guard.ts:87-118 — The guard misses destructuring/aliasing/namespace access of Date and Math even when it does run.
  Why: `classify` only flags a `PropertyAccessExpression` whose object is the bare `Identifier` "Date"/"Math" (lines 89-95), and `CallExpression`/`NewExpression` whose callee is the bare `Identifier` "Date" (lines 101-118). All of the following escape every branch and pass `assertDeterministic` while still reading wall-clock time or randomness: `const { now } = Date; now();` (callee is "now", not "Date"), `const r = Math.random; r();`, `globalThis.Date.now()` (object is a `PropertyAccessExpression`, not `Identifier`), and `const D = Date; new D();`. The module header claims it "reject[s] any reference to the four non-deterministic APIs"; it does not. A smuggled call destabilizes the cache key exactly as in finding 1. (The header documents the transitive-import gap but not this same-file aliasing gap.)
  Fix: Also flag (a) any value-position `Identifier` whose text is `Date`/`Math` (catches `const {now}=Date`, `const D=Date`), and (b) any `PropertyAccessExpression` whose `.name.text` is `now`/`random` regardless of the object expression (catches `globalThis.Date.now`).

3. [minor] src/runner/stage-executor.ts:127,160 — The runner hashes the whole `AgentStep` as the cache signature, contradicting `key.ts`'s documented contract.
  Why: `execAgent` calls `dispatchAgentCall(callId, prompt, step, exec)` (line 160), and `dispatchAgentCall` passes that object straight to `computeCacheKey({ ..., signature })` (line 127). `computeCacheKey` → `stabilize` sorts and keeps every enumerable field, so `id`, `type:"agent"`, `retry`, and (when `prompt` is a string rather than a function) the prompt itself are folded into the sha256. `key.ts` (lines 35-37, 54-58) defines `AgentCacheSignature` as exactly `{ model, tools, systemPrompt }` and states the "caller constructs this explicitly so callId/signal/cwd … never leak into the key by accident." No correctness bug today (all leaked fields are deterministic and identical-prompt/different-id just reduces sharing), but it violates the stated key contract, and any future non-deterministic field added to `AgentStep` would silently corrupt cache keys.
  Fix: Build the signature explicitly at the call site — `const signature: AgentCacheSignature = { model: step.model, tools: step.tools, systemPrompt: step.systemPrompt }` — before `computeCacheKey`, and do the same in the fan_out/loop_until/composite dispatch sites that feed `dispatchAgentCall`.

All findings verified against source. Here is my audit.

---

1. **[MAJOR]** `test/ast-guard.test.ts:31-77` — the "reject banned APIs" suite only covers the four exact syntactic forms the guard hardcodes; trivial evasions pass the guard with zero coverage.
   Why: `classify` (`src/determinism/ast-guard.ts:87-114`) matches *only* a `PropertyAccessExpression` whose object is a bare `Identifier` (`Date.now`, `Math.random`), a bare `Date()` `CallExpression`, and a `new Date()` `NewExpression`. I verified by execution that `Date["now"]()`, `globalThis.Date.now()`, `Math["random"]()`, and `new (Date)()` all return **0** violations. No negative test asserts any of these is rejected, so the guard's incompleteness is invisible to the suite. A workflow body using `Date["now"]()` sails past the loader guard (`src/loader.ts`) → its output (and the cache key derived from it) is non-deterministic → resume never hits → the engine's core determinism/cache-resume guarantee is silently broken. This is the dimension's named "AST guard evasion" gap.
   Fix: add negative cases to `ast-guard.test.ts` asserting `findDeterminismViolations` flags `Date["now"]()`, `Math["random"]()`, `globalThis.Date.now()`, and `new (Date)()` (these will currently fail, exposing the src hole in `classify` to also handle `ElementAccessExpression` and nested-receiver property access).

2. **[MAJOR]** `test/abort.test.ts:13-24,47-52,91-95` + `test/e2e/helpers.ts:53-76` — the real abort→subprocess-kill path is never executed by any test; the mocks substitute for it and assert it by absence.
   Why: `abortAgent`/`skipAgent`/`retryAgent` only abort the per-call `AbortController`. The actual SIGTERM→SIGKILL translation lives solely in `spawnAgent`'s `killProc` listener (`sessions/spawn.ts:317-329`), which is reached only via the default `spawnAgent` dispatch. Every abort test uses `fakeRegistry` with mock processes and asserts `proc.kill` is **not** called (`abort.test.ts:50-52,95`) on the strength of an unverified comment ("kill is spawn listener's job"). Every e2e abort scenario injects `makeFakeDispatch`, which links the controller and returns a canned `abortedResult` but never spawns a process nor touches `registry.processes` (`helpers.ts:59-76`). Consequently scenario 5's `expect(registry.processes.size).toBe(0)` is **vacuously true** — the fake never populates `processes`, so it cannot detect a process-leak or no-kill regression. If the `addEventListener("abort", killProc)` wiring or the 5s SIGKILL escalation broke, no test would fail. This is precisely "mocks hide real bugs" for the abort guarantee.
   Fix: add a real-subprocess abort test (e.g. spawn a `sleep`-style child the runner actually kills, or at minimum assert `makeFakeDispatch`/the fake registry records a kill on abort) and stop asserting `processes.size === 0` against a registry the fake never populates.

3. **[MAJOR]** `test/journal.test.ts:25-54` — the journal's concurrent-append serialization (the reason `appendChain` exists) is untested, and no test reloads a journal written by a parallel `fan_out`.
   Why: `Journal.append` chains writes onto `appendChain` (`src/cache/journal.ts:71-79`) specifically because concurrent `appendFile` calls interleave bytes for entries > PIPE_BUF, and `load` then silently drops the corrupted lines (`journal.ts:42-46`). `fan_out` dispatches agents concurrently, each appending `started`+`result` via `dispatchAgentCall` (`stage-executor.ts:131,150`), so this is a live production path. Every append in `journal.test.ts` is sequential. The save/reload e2e (scenario 4) uses a single agent; cache-resume (scenario 6) uses two *sequential* agents. The exact scenario where corruption would surface on resume — a parallel `fan_out` followed by reload — has no test, so the on-disk integrity invariant that makes cache-replay sound is unverified.
   Fix: add a test that fires `N` concurrent `append` calls and asserts `load` recovers all `N` after a fresh `Journal`, plus an e2e that runs a `fan_out` (parallelism>1), then re-runs in a new process/journal and asserts zero re-dispatch with all items intact.

4. **[MAJOR]** `test/e2e/scenarios.test.ts:124-147` + `test/e2e/composites.test.ts` — `maxTokens` exhaustion mid-run (the `guardSpawn` path) has no integration test; only the `maxAgents` pre-check is covered.
   Why: `guardBatch` (`stage-executor.ts:513-518`) pre-checks a whole batch but calls only `assertBatchSize` + `canSpawn`, and `canSpawn` consults the **agents** headroom alone — not tokens. `maxTokens` is enforced *only* by `guardSpawn`'s `isExhausted` (`stage-executor.ts:520-525`), invoked per-agent at `stage-executor.ts:134`. Every e2e budget test uses `maxAgents` (`scenarios.test.ts:127`; the adversarial budget regression), which routes through `guardBatch`. `maxTokens` appears only in `test/budget.test.ts` unit tests. The runner refusing a mid-flight spawn when the token budget is drained (tokens summed in `applyOutcome` at `stage-executor.ts:528-532`, then `isExhausted` tripping on the next `guardSpawn`) → `BudgetExceededError` → step failed is entirely untested at the integration level.
   Fix: add an e2e with `budget: { maxTokens: <small> }` where the fake dispatch's per-call token cost exhausts the pool after the first agent, and assert the run fails with a budget error on a later spawn (not a pre-check).

5. **[MINOR]** `test/budget.test.ts:43-57` — `isExhausted`'s `agents === 0` disjunct is never exercised.
   Why: the suite tests `isExhausted` for `tokens === 0` (line 43) and `durationMs === 0` (line 49) and the no-cap case (line 55), but `BudgetPool.isExhausted` (`src/budget/pool.ts`) also returns true when the agents cap is spent. That branch — the one `guardSpawn` relies on to refuse spawns under `maxAgents` — has no direct test; a regression flipping `||` to `&&` or dropping the agents term would not be caught at the unit level.
   Fix: add `new BudgetPool({ maxAgents: 2 }, 0); p.track({ agents: 2 }); expect(p.isExhausted(0)).toBe(true);`.

6. **[MINOR]** `test/outcomes-planner.test.ts:57-62` — the "runnable-shaped" test asserts only `name` and `steps.length`, leaving the `evaluate` keyword routing unverified.
   Why: `heuristicallyPlan("evaluate the design")` is meant to route to `adversarial` via the `\b(...|evaluate)\b` alternation (`src/planner.ts`), but the test never asserts `wf.steps[0].type`. Only `review`→`adversarial` is asserted (line 35-40). If the regex dropped `evaluate` (or `versus`/`competing`/`categor`/`dispatch`), this test would still pass — a weak assertion that documents an exercise rather than an outcome.
   Fix: assert `wf.steps[0].type === "adversarial"` (and cover the remaining alternation branches `versus`/`vs`/`best of`/`categor`/`route`/`dispatch` with one case each).

I've read all assigned files in full (stage-executor.ts, runner/index.ts, budget/pool.ts, budget/caps.ts, lifecycle.ts, planner.ts) plus types.ts, and the supporting spawn.ts/journal.ts/outcomes.ts needed to verify findings. Here are my substantiated findings.

---

1. **[SEVERITY: major] src/runner/stage-executor.ts:134,152 + src/budget/pool.ts:75,81 — `maxTokens` budget cap is silently exceeded under any concurrent fan_out/composite; the per-spawn guard is a check-then-act race with no reservation.**
   Why: `guardSpawn` (stage-executor.ts:520) only *reads* `pool.isExhausted()`/`canSpawn()`; the actual spend is recorded later in `applyOutcome` (line 528, `pool.track(...)`). Between the check (line 134) and the track (line 152) lie two `await`s — `journal.append` (136) and `dispatch` (138–141). In `execFanOut` (200–214) all `parallelism` workers enter `dispatchAgentCall` synchronously and each runs guardSpawn→`await journal.append` before yielding, so every worker passes the guard against identical stale pool state; only afterward do they settle and call `applyOutcome`. Compounding this, `guardBatch` (513–517) calls only `canSpawn` which checks the *agents* dimension exclusively (pool.ts:80–82), and `isExhausted` (pool.ts:74–76) returns true only when a dimension hits *exactly* 0 — so a call costing 10k tokens passes while `remaining.tokens` is still 1. Concrete failure: `maxTokens:1000`, no `maxAgents`, `fan_out` of 8 items → `guardBatch` passes (`canSpawn(8)` → ∞ ≥ 8), all 8 workers pass `guardSpawn`, all 8 dispatch, total spend = 8 × per-agent tokens, exceeding the cap by ~8× with no error thrown. The budget-aware `scaleBatchByBudget` (pool.ts:94) that was designed to prevent exactly this is never invoked by the executor. The file header (line 20) claims "maxTokens is enforced via BudgetPool.isExhausted on each spawn" — under concurrency that claim is false.
   Fix: Reserve the agent headroom atomically in `guardSpawn` (increment a pending counter before the first `await`, decrement in `applyOutcome`/error paths), and call `scaleBatchByBudget` in `execFanOut`/`execAdversarial`/`execTournament` to cap the batch by remaining token budget given an estimated per-agent cost. At minimum, document `maxTokens` as advisory under `parallelism > 1`.

2. **[SEVERITY: minor] src/cache/journal.ts:79 — a single `appendFile` rejection permanently poisons `appendChain`; every subsequent journal write silently no-ops and the run fails step-by-step.**
   Why: `this.appendChain = this.appendChain.then(() => fs.promises.appendFile(...))`. If one `appendFile` rejects (transient disk/permission/ENOSPC), the chain promise stays rejected; every later `.then` callback is *skipped* (not invoked), so later `append` calls return a rejected promise without ever attempting the write. Meanwhile the in-memory `results.set` on line 77 still runs before the write, so memory and disk diverge. This cascades into stage-executor.ts: every `dispatchAgentCall` does `await exec.journal.append(...)` (lines 136 and 155) outside any try/catch, so each subsequent agent call throws → `runStepSequence` fails the step → the whole run dies from one transient I/O error, even after the disk recovers.
   Fix: decouple prior failures from future writes: `const prev = this.appendChain.catch(() => {}); this.appendChain = prev.then(() => fs.promises.appendFile(...));` so a single failed write doesn't block subsequent ones.

3. **[SEVERITY: minor] src/runner/stage-executor.ts:260,304,513–517 — `guardBatch` assumes every sub-call will dispatch, so on retry of a composite it demands full headroom even when most sub-calls are cache hits, falsely failing near-budget workflows.**
   Why: `execAdversarial` calls `guardBatch(exec, 1 + judgeCount)` and `execTournament` calls `guardBatch(exec, candidates + judges)` *before* any `dispatchAgentCall`. On retry (via `runWithRetry`, 467–478), successful sub-calls from the prior attempt are replayed from the journal cache (dispatchAgentCall short-circuits at line 132 before `guardSpawn`), so they consume no budget — but `guardBatch` still demands `total` agents of headroom. Concrete scenario: adversarial with 1 produce + 3 judges, `maxAgents: 6`; first attempt dispatches all 4 (produce ok, 2 judges ok and cached, 1 judge fails) → `spentAgents = 4`; retry calls `guardBatch(4)` with `remaining.agents = 2` → `canSpawn(4)` is false → throws `BudgetExceededError`, aborting the step, even though the retry only needs to re-dispatch the single failed judge (1 agent, and 2 ≥ 1).
   Fix: make `guardBatch` cache-aware (count expected misses by probing `journal.lookup` per sub-call), or drop the budget clause from `guardBatch` and rely on the per-call `guardSpawn` (already called after the cache check) — keeping `guardBatch` only for the `MAX_BATCH` assertion.
